editorial_intro: Pixar's Toy Story 5 still owns the multiplex, but the diaspora's spoiled for choice this weekend: Akshay Kumar's 25-star Welcome to the Jungle and the Gippy Grewal Punjabi juggernaut Carry on Jatta 4 both land wide, while Ram Charan's Peddi and Samantha's Maa Inti Bangaaram keep South cinema packing overseas houses. Add Supergirl's DC swing and Spielberg's Disclosure Day, and there's no excuse to stay home.

movies.title: Toy Story 5
movies.why_watch: Woody, Buzz and the gang are back after more than a decade, and this time the enemy is a screen, not a villain. It crushed its opening weekend at $214M and is still the undisputed king of the multiplex. You'll cry harder than the kids.

movies.title: Welcome To The Jungle
movies.why_watch: The third Welcome film is a 25-plus star circus, and the verdict is in: leave logic at home and let the chaos win. Taran Adarsh calls it 'entertaining,' fans say they couldn't stop laughing, and there's no better place to see it than a packed diaspora theater on opening weekend.

movies.title: Carry On Jatta 4
movies.why_watch: The fourth chapter of Pollywood's funniest franchise, and a tearjerker behind the camera: late comedy legend Jaswinder Bhalla returns as Advocate Dhillon via a six-month VFX recreation made with his family's blessing. Goosebump nostalgia plus the trademark misunderstanding-driven mayhem. A Punjabi-cinema event, not just a movie.

movies.title: Supergirl
movies.why_watch: Milly Alcock's hard-living, foul-mouthed Kara Zor-El takes a cosmic road trip alongside Jason Momoa's bounty hunter Lobo, with a David Corenswet Superman cameo. Critics call it 'fine' rather than great, but Gillespie (I, Tonya; Cruella) swings for a grittier, weirder DC than Superman. Worth a look if you want the big-screen spectacle.

movies.title: Peddi
movies.why_watch: Ram Charan's rugged comeback as a lower-caste village cricketer-turned-wrestler fighting for his people's dignity, scored by A.R. Rahman. The writing is uneven, but the highest-grossing Telugu film of the year has already crossed $3M in North America. Go for the scale, the Rahman soundtrack, and a fired-up Charan.

movies.title: Maa Inti Bangaaram
movies.why_watch: Samantha flips the 'perfect housewife' trope on its head as a homemaker with a deadly secret past, in a 90s-set thriller producer Raj Nidimoru says resonated harder than Stree or The Family Man. The second half wobbles, but Samantha carries the whole film, and it's already past ₹50 crore worldwide. Her show, start to finish.

movies.title: Disclosure Day
movies.why_watch: Spielberg's first alien movie since War of the Worlds is a government-conspiracy thriller critics are calling his best sci-fi since Close Encounters. It opened at #1 and Emily Blunt is already drawing Oscar buzz. Pure big-screen Spielberg.

movies.title: Cocktail 2
movies.why_watch: Fourteen years on, Homi Adajania revives Bollywood's defining urban rom-com with Shahid, Kriti and Rashmika in a messy modern love triangle, and a Pritam soundtrack already on repeat. Critics are calling it a winner. The diaspora date-night pick of the summer.

movies.title: Main Vaapas Aaunga
movies.why_watch: Imtiaz Ali + A.R. Rahman + Diljit + Naseeruddin Shah in a Partition-era love story spanning 78 years. Naseer's turn as a dementia-stricken patriarch is being called career-defining. Bring tissues; this one lingers.

movies.title: Pressure
movies.why_watch: A D-Day thriller where the battle is over weather forecasts, not beaches. Brendan Fraser as Eisenhower and Andrew Scott as the meteorologist who saved the invasion. CinemaScore: A. A quietly gripping watch.

movies.title: The Furious
movies.rating: Critics' 'Best of the Year' action pick
movies.why_watch: The action film that united critics and fans this year. Choreographer-turned-director Kenji Tanigaki delivers bone-crunching, wall-to-wall combat in the tradition of The Raid. Limited US screens, so hunt it down; it's destined to be a martial-arts cult classic.

movies.title: Backrooms
movies.why_watch: A24's highest-grossing film ever, directed by a 20-year-old YouTube creator. A creepypasta turned liminal nightmare that makes empty hallways and fluorescent lights genuinely terrifying. The internet's horror canon goes mainstream.
